content.title: School Resource Officers
content.summary: The School Resource Officer (SRO) program assigns officers to specific schools to foster a safe environment for students, acting as liaisons between the police, school, and community. SROs mentor students, engage with parents and teachers, and serve as role models. Additionally, the Safe2Tell initiative allows individuals to report concerns anonymously to help prevent violence in schools.
content.body:
The School Resource Officer program dedicates an officer to the needs of a particular school's community.

SROs act as a liaison between the police department, school, and community. Their mission is to provide a safe, secure environment where students can thrive. SROs mentor students and present information in the classroom. They also meet with parents and teachers. SROs are often role models for students, giving them sound advice and encouraging feelings of self-worth.

## Elementary Schools

- Elementary schools on a rotating basis

## Middle Schools

- Prospect Academy - Officer Matt Ortega
- Three Creeks Kindergarten to 8th - Officer Kelly Lechuga
- North Arvada Middle School - Officer Kevin Lewis
- Oberon Middle School - Officer Adrienne Blackwood

## High Schools

- Arvada High School - Officer Matt Ortega and Officer Albino Guerrero
- Arvada West High School - Officer Craig Smith
- Ralston Valley High School - Officer Nicole Deering
- Pomona High School - Officer Richard Brown

## Safe2Tell

Make a Call. Make a Difference. 1-877-542-7233 (SAFE)

Safe2Tell provides students and adults in all Colorado schools and communities an increased ability to both prevent and report violence by making safe, **anonymous** calls.
